notes.summary: Number System covers types of numbers, place value, divisibility rules, HCF and LCM, remainders, unit digits, factors and recurring decimals. SSC CGL asks 2-3 questions from it in every paper, mainly on remainders, unit digits, divisibility and HCF/LCM applications.
keyPoints: Divisibility by 11: (sum of digits at odd places from the right) − (sum at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11. 737561 → (1 + 5 + 3) − (6 + 7 + 7) = −11, so it is divisible. By 8: the last three digits must be divisible by 8.

Unit digits repeat in cycles of 4: 2 → 2, 4, 8, 6; 3 → 3, 9, 7, 1; 7 → 7, 9, 3, 1; 8 → 8, 4, 2, 6. Digits 0, 1, 5, 6 never change; 4 and 9 cycle in 2. Divide the power by 4 and use the remainder (remainder 0 means the 4th term).

Write N as a product of prime powers. Number of factors = product of (each power + 1); sum of factors = product of (1 + p + p² + ...) for each prime. 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5 → 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 factors, sum = 15 × 13 × 6 = 1170.
Greatest number that divides x and y leaving remainders r1 and r2 = HCF of (x − r1) and (y − r2).
Least number leaving the same remainder r when divided by several numbers = LCM × k + r; choose the smallest k that meets any extra condition.
If N leaves remainder r when divided by d, and m is a factor of d, then N leaves the same remainder as r does when divided by m (342 = 18 × 19, so remainder 47 by 342 → 47 ÷ 18 → 11).
aⁿ + bⁿ is divisible by (a + b) when n is odd; aⁿ − bⁿ is always divisible by (a − b), and also by (a + b) when n is even.
HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators/LCM of denominators; LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators/HCF of denominators.
Place value depends on position, face value is the digit itself. In 857326 the digit 7 has place value 7000 and face value 7.
traps: Treating remainder 0 in a unit-digit cycle as the 1st term instead of the 4th.
Mixing up HCF and LCM: 'greatest number that divides' needs HCF, 'least number divisible by' needs LCM.
Calling 1 a prime number; it is neither prime nor composite, and 2 is the only even prime.
For the LCM of fractions, taking the LCM of the denominators instead of their HCF.
Forgetting to subtract the given remainders before finding the HCF.
notes.examTip: In remainder and divisibility questions, test the options directly when the algebra looks long; most wrong options fail a quick divisibility check.

questions.text: Which fraction is equal to the recurring decimal 0.454545... (45 repeating)?
questions.explanation:
For two repeating digits, 0.ababab... = ab/99.
0.4545... = 45/99.
Dividing numerator and denominator by 9: 45/99 = 5/11.

questions.text: What is the difference between the place value and the face value of 7 in the number 857326?
questions.explanation:
In 857326, the digit 7 is in the thousands place.
Place value = 7 × 1000 = 7000; face value = 7.
Difference = 7000 − 7 = 6993.

questions.text: What is the smallest number by which 1800 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
questions.explanation:
1800 = 2³ × 3² × 5².
In a perfect square every prime has an even power; only 2 has an odd power (3).
Multiply by 2: 1800 × 2 = 3600 = 60².

questions.text: If the six-digit number 73k561 is divisible by 11, what is the value of the digit k?
questions.explanation:
Rule for 11: (sum of digits at odd places from the right) − (sum at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11.
Odd places (1, 5, 3) = 9; even places (6, k, 7) = 13 + k.
9 − (13 + k) = −(4 + k) must be a multiple of 11, so 4 + k = 11.
k = 7 (737561 = 11 × 67051).

questions.text: What is the unit digit of 3⁶⁵ × 6⁵⁹ × 7⁷¹?
questions.explanation:
3 has the cycle 3, 9, 7, 1; 65 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 1, so 3⁶⁵ ends in 3.
6 raised to any power ends in 6.
7 has the cycle 7, 9, 3, 1; 71 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 3, so 7⁷¹ ends in 3.
Unit digit = 3 × 6 × 3 = 54, so the answer is 4.

questions.text: What is the greatest number that divides 1657 and 2037 leaving remainders 6 and 5 respectively?
questions.explanation:
Subtract the remainders: 1657 − 6 = 1651 and 2037 − 5 = 2032.
Required number = HCF(1651, 2032).
1651 = 13 × 127 and 2032 = 16 × 127, and 13 and 16 have no common factor.
HCF = 127.

questions.text: A number when divided by 342 leaves a remainder of 47. What will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 18?
questions.explanation:
Write the number as 342q + 47. Since 342 = 18 × 19, the part 342q is exactly divisible by 18.
So only 47 matters: 47 = 18 × 2 + 11.
Required remainder = 11.

questions.text: What is the sum of all the factors of 360?
What is the LCM of 2/3, 4/9 and 5/6?
questions.explanation:
LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators/HCF of denominators.
LCM(2, 4, 5) = 20 and HCF(3, 9, 6) = 3.
LCM = 20/3. (1/18 is their HCF, not LCM.)

questions.text: What is the remainder when (17²³ + 23²³) is divided by 40?
questions.explanation:
Rule: aⁿ + bⁿ is exactly divisible by (a + b) when n is odd.
Here a + b = 17 + 23 = 40 and n = 23 is odd.
So 17²³ + 23²³ is divisible by 40, and the remainder is 0.

questions.text: What is the least number which, when divided by 5, 6, 7 and 8, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case, but is exactly divisible by 9?
questions.explanation:
LCM(5, 6, 7, 8) = 840, so the number has the form 840k + 3.
840 ÷ 9 leaves remainder 3, so 840k + 3 leaves the same remainder as 3k + 3 when divided by 9.
3k + 3 must be divisible by 9; the smallest such k is 2.
Number = 840 × 2 + 3 = 1683 (1683 ÷ 9 = 187).
